selection.rule: Select every test case registered by the current mlibc ANSI, POSIX, Linux, Linux-wrapper, and RTLD Meson declarations. ANSI, POSIX, and RTLD are active because the WOS mlibc configuration enables their required option surface. Linux and Linux-wrapper cases remain selected but are reviewed unsupported because WOS declares linux_option unsupported; active-suite cases whose required WosSysdepTags or compiler features are absent are also reviewed unsupported rather than discovered from runtime failures.

WOS does not expose the mlibc GetParam or SetParam scheduler sysdeps; the generic API therefore returns ENOSYS by design.
mlibc's nice() implementation requires the Nice sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose; WOS priority get/set coverage remains separate.
mlibc's pause() path requires the Pause sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose; Sigsuspend coverage remains separate.
WOS does not expose the mlibc TimerCreate, TimerSettime, TimerGettime, or TimerDelete sysdeps.
Cross-thread pthread cancellation requires the Tgkill sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose.
pthread_kill() dispatches through the Tgkill sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose.
WOS does not expose the mlibc per-thread GetSchedparam or SetSchedparam sysdeps.
WOS does not expose the mlibc GetScheduler or SetScheduler policy sysdeps; priority APIs are covered separately.
Queued signal values require the Sigqueue sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose.
The case wakes sigsuspend through pthread_kill(), which requires the absent Tgkill sysdep even though WOS exposes Sigsuspend itself.
Synchronous timed signal dequeue requires the Sigtimedwait sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose.
Populating POSIX siginfo_t child status requires the Waitid sysdep, which WosSysdepTags does not expose; waitpid remains covered.
